# Fixed auth-envelope v1/v2 compatibility vectors

These files are **frozen compatibility test data**. They are checked-in
golden bytes for the version 1 (`auth_wrap` / `auth_unwrap`) and version 2
(`auth_state_wrap` / `auth_state_unwrap` / `auth_state_fingerprint`)
authenticated envelope formats and must never be regenerated by the test
suite.

## Shared authentication key

- `auth_key.bin` — the non-secret shared test key, the 27 ASCII bytes
  `b"pqattest-auth-compat-key/v1"`. Every envelope tag and every state
  fingerprint below is keyed with exactly this value. It is public test
  material, not a real secret.

## Wrapped payloads (plaintext inner formats)

Each payload is a legal output of an existing public serialiser, produced
from the deterministic public inputs listed further below:

- `payload_lamport.bin` — `OneTimeSigner.checkpoint()` of an unused
  Lamport signer (`bits=32`, magic `b"PQALCP\0\0"`).
- `payload_wots.bin` — `WOTSOneTimeSigner.checkpoint()` of an unused
  W-OTS signer (`w=4`, magic `b"PQAWCP\0\0"`).
- `payload_merkle_initial.bin` — `MerkleSigner.checkpoint()` of a fresh
  Merkle signer (`height=2`, `w=4`, `next_index = 0`, magic
  `b"PQAMSCP\0"`).
- `payload_merkle_spent.bin` — `checkpoint()` of a second signer built
  from the same Merkle key input after signing the fixed message
  `b"compat-auth-merkle"` once (`next_index = 1`). Together with
  `payload_merkle_initial.bin` this gives two different legal payloads of
  one scheme, wrapped below at the *same* generation.
- `payload_lattice.bin` — `ToyLatticePrivateKey.to_bytes()` of the
  deterministic toy-lattice key (magic `b"PQALSK\0\0"`).

## v1 envelopes (`auth_wrap`, version byte 1)

One per scheme, each wrapping the payload above under `auth_key.bin`:

- `v1_lamport.bin`, `v1_wots.bin`, `v1_merkle.bin` (wraps
  `payload_merkle_initial.bin`), `v1_lattice.bin`.

## v2 envelopes (`auth_state_wrap`, version byte 2) and fingerprints

The set as a whole covers generation zero, one ordinary positive
generation and the maximum `2**64 - 1`; not every scheme is wrapped at
every generation.

- `v2_lamport_g0.bin` — lamport payload at generation `0`.
- `v2_wots_g7.bin` — wots payload at generation `7`.
- `v2_merkle_initial_g3.bin` — initial merkle payload at generation `3`.
- `v2_merkle_spent_g3.bin` — spent merkle payload at generation `3`
  (same generation, different payload: the state-binding pair).
- `v2_lattice_gmax.bin` — lattice payload at generation `2**64 - 1`.

- `fingerprint_<name>.bin` — the 32-byte
  `auth_state_fingerprint(envelope, key)` of the matching `v2_<name>.bin`
  envelope, i.e. `HMAC-SHA-256(key, b"pqattest/auth-state-id/v1" + body)`
  over the envelope body (all bytes before the 32-byte tag).

## Deterministic public inputs

All inputs are fixed, public, non-secret test values, all drawn through
the public key-generation entries:

- Lamport: `keygen(bits=32, token_bytes=...)` where the Nth call returns
  the integer N as a 32-byte big-endian value (1, 2, 3, ...).
- W-OTS: `wots_keygen(w=4, token_bytes=...)` with the same counter rule.
- Merkle: `MerkleSigner(height=2, w=4, token_bytes=...)` with the same
  counter rule; the spent payload additionally signs the fixed message
  `b"compat-auth-merkle"` once on leaf 0.
- Toy lattice: `toy_lattice_keygen(token_bytes=...)` whose single call
  returns the eight ASCII bytes `b"compat-k"`.

The exact bytes were produced once by a standalone script using the
baseline encoder and are now fixed; tests only read them. If a future
change to the v1/v2 envelope layouts, the HMAC coverage, the fingerprint
domain separator or the scheme identifier table makes any of these bytes
mismatch, that is the compatibility break the regression test exists to
catch — it must not be silently fixed by relaxing parsing or
regenerating these files.
